correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer ell>=2 and s>=2 the event M_s=u_j and multiplicity a has exact count p_ell(n-s S_{j-1}-a u_j)-p_ell(n-s S_{j-1}-(a+1)u_j). This is obtained by mandatory-copy removal and exclusion of extra u_j. Summing a telescopes to p_ell(n). Pairwise difference of the corresponding q generating factors has cancellation to order two; with rho=1-1/ell, the analytic Gaussian sum equals (b-a) sqrt(pi/2) t^(1/2)/(s^(3/2) sqrt(rho)) +O(t), while the restricted partition Euler product has exponential parameter mu=pi^2 rho/6. Cauchy coefficient extraction at t=sqrt(mu/n) gives the signed n^-1/4 mark difference; the proof gives direct trigonometric product bounds off the principal saddle, not merely formal substitution or subtraction of two weak o(1) limits. Sum of probabilities fixes the intercept. The equality M_r=M_s iff J_s<r establishes the positive tie correction. The exact partition-enumeration checker was run from the local package and passed 300 direct enumerations and 27 large-n comparisons. The finite tests are supplementary, not proof. All boundaries, quantifiers, constants and claimed limits match the proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the explicit signed order-n^-1/4 distribution among all s deficiency marks for ell-regular partitions and the resulting sharp positive tie-probability correction. The November 2026 motivating paper marks least-gap location and provides selected aggregate asymptotics, not the stopping multiplicity. Wagner 2011 gives the leading one-gap local limit for general part sets. The published November 8 regular-gap note gives a leading joint weak law but no first marked finite-size coefficient, and the October 25 unrestricted note gives a uniform-mark leading limit, not the signed correction. Distinct implications were compared at full-text level: none establishes the signed coefficient or exact sharp bias. An unindexed stronger asymptotic remains possible but is not shown by these sources.
residual_risks: Potential unindexed second-order marked local limit for general Meinardus part sequences could subsume the signed coefficient.
Related older partition-statistics literature may contain an implicit marked expansion even if not named as a least-gap theorem.

value.rationale: A natural recently studied first-deficiency statistic has a uniform leading multiplicity mark, masking a systematic signed finite-size effect. The complete profile for all permitted marks and every fixed ell,s has strict linear ordering, an explicit nonzero universal-in-form amplitude and a first sharp correction for the probability that two ranks coalesce. It is neither a routine restatement of the leading Rayleigh limit nor an arbitrary finite numerical slice. Its full first-correction spectrum can serve as a quantitative benchmark for finer partition statistics.
